name: TPA6120A2 (TI dual current-feedback headphone amplifier)
tagline: TI's 2004 stereo current-feedback headphone driver, rated at 128 dB dynamic range and 1300 V/µs. Its current drive powered the Xonar Essence STX and many DAC/amps.
technology: Dual (stereo) current-feedback amplifier (CFA) headphone driver. Split supply of ±5 V to ±15 V; TI's product page gives the total supply range as 9 V to 33 V. PowerPAD packages: 20-pin SOIC (DWP, listed by TI as HSOIC) and 14-pin VQFN (RGY). Surface-mount only, with no DIP version.

reputation.summary: TI's ready-made current-feedback headphone driver was widely used in the 2009-2016 PC-audio and Chinese DAC/amp boom. Examples: the Asus Xonar Essence STX, Musiland Monitor sound cards, FiiO E9, and Sony PHA-1/PHA-2. It remains in current DAC/amps (SMSL, Sabaj, Aiyima, WiiM, FiiO, Shanling). Enthusiasts value its strong current drive, very low datasheet noise and distortion, and low cost. DIYers often use it as the output stage of an op-amp + CFA composite loop, e.g. OPA1602/OPA1612 + TPA6120A2 on diyAudio. Soomal tested 10-16 products using it and stresses that results depend heavily on the implementation. Measured results are mixed: designs with series output resistors show about 10 Ω output impedance (ASR on Sony PHA-1; Roland UA-M10), while well-executed composite designs measure very well.
sonic_descriptors: coarse or lacking finesse in a high-output-impedance implementation (Soomal, Sabaj A20d 2022)
typical_uses: Sound-card headphone outputs: Asus Xonar Essence STX/ST, Creative Sound Blaster ZxR / E5 / X7 / BlasterX G5, Musiland Monitor series
Portable amps and DAPs: Sony PHA-1 / PHA-2, OPPO HA-2, FiiO E9 and X7 AM5 module, Topping NX3, Shanling M5 Ultra
Desktop DAC/amps: SMSL SAP-9 / M20 / DO400, Sabaj A20d, Aiyima DAC-A10, WiiM Ultra, Roland UA-M10, Rupert Neve RNHP
Current buffer inside a VFA-CFA composite loop (OPA1602/OPA1612, OPA2134, NE5532)
DIY headphone amp boards (pavouk.org, Cocoacrumbs, Head-Fi and AMB threads)
caveats: TI's typical application uses series output resistors, so many products have high output impedance, e.g. about 10 Ω on Sony PHA-1 (ASR) and Roland UA-M10.
Very high drive can damage low-impedance headphones or IEMs if gain is not limited (Soomal warning on the Musiland Monitor 01 PS).
Very wide-bandwidth CFA: sensitive to layout, feedback-resistor value and capacitive loads. Composite loops need careful compensation. Gain-setting questions are common on TI E2E.
The PowerPAD must be soldered to a thermal via array.
Surface-mount only (PowerPAD SOIC-20 / VQFN-14), so it cannot be swapped in a DIP socket.
Needs rails of ±5 V to ±15 V. Portable designs need boost converters, and Soomal reports it performs better at higher supply voltage.

counterfeit_notes: No documented counterfeit or remarked TPA6120A2 reports were found. Loose chips are sold mostly through AliExpress/Taobao modules and kits, so their supply chain cannot be verified. Buy from TI or authorized distributors (Mouser 595-TPA6120A2DWPR / 595-TPA6120A2RGYT, DigiKey, LCSC C70439). The practical checks are a genuine TI top mark with date code and an intact exposed PowerPAD.

revision_chain_notes:
Texas Instruments SLOS431 (TPA6120A2 datasheet; TI is the sole source, with no acquirer or second-source editions). The known chain, oldest to newest, is complete:

- SLOS431, original, March 2004. Copies: the Digi-Key media copy, plus probably the octopart DWPG4 cache and the new datasheets.b-cdn.net TPA6120A2DWP cache, which have old-template all-caps FEATURES/DESCRIPTION/APPLICATIONS headings.
- SLOS431A, 'MARCH 2004 - REVISED JULY 2014'.
- SLOS431B, 'MARCH 2004 - REVISED FEBRUARY 2015', the current edition at ti.com symlink and /lit/ds/slos431b/.

No revision C or later appeared in any search.

Missing links:
1. No URL was found for a copy confirmed to hold SLOS431A. A search for "SLOS431A" returned only the product page and already-listed mirrors, with no revision header shown. The octopart RGYT and LCSC copies have new-template titles ('Filter and I/V Gain Stage Stereo Hi-Fi Headphone Driver ... DYR > 120 dB'), so each could hold A or B, but the summaries do not show which.
2. The change lists for A and B were not retrieved. A 'Changes from Original / Changes from Revision A' search found nothing.
3. No copy was confirmed to show the literal 'SLOS431 - MARCH 2004' footer. The original is only inferred from the old template.

Related document: SLOU169 (HPA Audio Power / TPA6120A2EVM User's Guide). It is dated May 2004 according to the search result title, and no later revision was seen.

The archive_seed_urls were derived from TI's standard legacy and revision-specific URL patterns (focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink, /lit/ds/<litnum>/<litnum>.pdf). They did not appear in the search results. They are only candidates for Wayback lookups (SLOS431 original and SLOS431A), not verified links.
